text:
ashley: quick PSA — after enabling per-request kernel routing weights for mixtral-8x we see improved throughput but a small QA/regression spike on eval-suite. low token divergence but steady wrong answer rate increase.

vikram: numbers?

ashley: profiling summary attached:
```
kernel_selector: policy=per-request-weighted
model: mixtral-8x
chosen_kernel: tiled_attn_v3
quant_path: 4bit-qlora
avg_latency_p50: 62ms -> 48ms (improved)
avg_latency_p95: 210ms -> 190ms
eval_answer_accuracy: 0.912 -> 0.869  # -4.3% absolute
kv_cache_consistency_checks: 0 failures -> 18 failures/10k
batch_skew: observed 3x variance in per-request seq lengths
```

ashley: the KV consistency failures line up with kernel swaps during a batch when requests have heterogeneous seq lengths. suspect tiled_attn_v3 uses a different kv layout/tiling that our cache-merge path mishandles under batch skew.

maria: is this reproducible locally? steps?

ashley: yes, small repro: run perf/regression/repro_mixtral_kv_swap.sh with seed=42. gist: 120 concurrent requests, seq lengths drawn from {64,512,2048}, enable per-request routing. Expect ~1-2 failures in 1k requests.

noah: can you paste the small trace where KV mismatch is detected?

ashley: trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 kernel=tiled_attn_v3 start_kv_write addr=0x7f8a... len=256
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] request_id=def456 kernel=fast_chunked_kernel start_kv_read addr=0x7f8a... len=128
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] kv_check: expected_head_dim=64 found_head_dim=32 -> mismatch
```

vikram: so two different kernels are writing/reading the same KV buffer with different head_dim packing. Oof. That explains wrong attention outputs.

maria: did we have a guard when routing kernels to ensure compatible kv layout? I thought kernel_selector had a compatibility matrix.

ashley: it does, but per-request weights allowed soft routing where fractional traffic goes to multiple kernels in the same batch. the batch-merge path assumes a single canonical kv layout for the whole batch. we missed the sanity check on mixed-kernel batches.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T14:05:00 by ashley: canary=eng-runtime/kernel-routing/weight-flag=true

ci-bot: ci/regression-run 9281: eval-suite/daily -> fail (accuracy drop reproducible), logs uploaded to /artifacts/9281

vikram: immediate mitigation options?

ashley: short-term: disable per-request weighted routing (rollback to deterministic kernel selection) — restores correctness but loses perf win (~+18% latency). mid-term: enforce kernel-compatibility grouping at batch assembly (reject mixing kernels with incompatible KV packing) + add unit tests. long-term: unify kv layout or implement on-the-fly reformat of KV segments (costly).

noah: add a small invariant check in batcher: if mixed kernels detected, split into two micro-batches instead of merging. That keeps perf while preserving correctness for common skew.

maria: sounds good. can you open a quick PR that: 1) flips the feature flag off in prod config, 2) adds the batching guard + test, 3) notes rollback rationale in release notes?

ashley: will do. creating PR and will post link. Also adding a short eval that runs KV-consistency checker across kernel variants post-merge.

vikram: follow-up: add a perf regression ticket to explore reformat cost vs latency gain. prioritize after fix.

ashley: agreed. logging action items:
- rollback per-request-weighted routing in prod flag (ashley)
- batching compatibility guard + unit tests (ashley/noah)
- eval-suite test for KV layout consistency (maria)
- perf analysis ticket (vikram)

maria: thanks — please ping when PR is up and when canary is reverted. :pray:

ashley: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4642 (WIP)

noah: thanks — nice catch. this was a subtle interaction between batching heuristics and kernel packing.

ashley: yup. learned that perf heuristics that route per-request need end-to-end invariants, not just per-kernel correctness. :helmet_with_cross:
